mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team A's shots FOR (recent vs. all-prior) AND shots_on_target FOR (recent vs. all-prior) simultaneously. Both observables must be evaluated together — a drop in shots combined with a drop in on-target ratio is a joint signal distinct from either alone. Compare resulting goal output against long-run goals FOR mean.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A goals FOR rises with the joint level of shots FOR and shots_on_target FOR; when both are simultaneously below long-run averages (as in recent-5 vs. all-prior here), goals FOR is suppressed relative to the long-run mean.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot volume (FOR) combined with its shots-on-target conversion rate (shots_on_target FOR / shots FOR) jointly predicts whether Team A's goal output rises above its long-run mean, beyond what either observable alone captures. Specifically, when a team's recent shot volume is declining while its on-target ratio is also declining, goal output is expected to be suppressed relative to the long-run average.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is not a single-observable mirror or a single observable with one band. It requires the joint relationship between two distinct offensive production observables (shots volume and on-target accuracy) and their combined effect on goals — neither observable alone captures the interaction.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team B's shots_on_target FOR (recent vs. all-prior) AND Team A's shots_on_target AGAINST (recent vs. all-prior). Both are elevated in the recent window. Measure whether the joint elevation of both observables — one team's attacking quality and the opponent's defensive concession rate — is associated with higher total goals AGAINST for Team A than either observable alone predicts.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both Team B's shots_on_target FOR (recent) and Team A's shots_on_target AGAINST (recent) are simultaneously elevated above their respective long-run means, goals AGAINST for Team A rises above what either single observable predicts independently.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shots-on-target FOR (recent) has risen relative to its long-run mean, while its goals FOR (recent) has also risen. The joint relationship between Team B's shots-on-target FOR and Team A's shots-on-target AGAINST (both elevated in recent windows) creates a combined attacking-vs-defensive pressure signal that is richer than either team's individual observable alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is an asymmetric cross-team joint relationship: it combines one team's attacking observable (Team B shots_on_target FOR) with the opponent's defensive observable (Team A shots_on_target AGAINST) simultaneously, which is not reducible to a single-observable mirror or a single band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Split corner_kicks FOR and AGAINST for Team A by half (FIRST_HALF vs. SECOND_HALF). Jointly evaluate the FOR–AGAINST differential within each half. Test whether the net corner deficit (AGAINST minus FOR) is larger in one half than the other, and whether this half-level asymmetry is consistent across the historical sample.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A's net corner deficit (corners AGAINST minus corners FOR) is larger in the first half than the second half, indicating a half-specific suppression of Team A's corner production that is not captured by full-match averages alone.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's corner kicks FOR exhibit a pronounced asymmetry between first-half and second-half production (FOR: 1H avg ~1.97, 2H avg ~2.19, all-prior), while Team A's corner kicks AGAINST are also split across halves (1H ~2.72, 2H ~2.69). The within-match half-level split of corner kicks FOR vs. AGAINST for Team A, conditioned jointly on both halves, reveals whether Team A's corner deficit (FOR vs. AGAINST) is concentrated in a specific half rather than uniformly distributed.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a within-match state split (half-level) combined with a joint FOR vs. AGAINST differential within each half — two dimensions simultaneously. It is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Split corner_kicks FOR and AGAINST for Team B by half (FIRST_HALF vs. SECOND_HALF). Jointly evaluate the FOR–AGAINST differential within each half. Test whether Team B's net corner concession (AGAINST minus FOR) is concentrated in the second half.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B's net corner concession (corners AGAINST minus corners FOR) is larger in the second half than the first half, indicating a second-half-specific vulnerability to opponent corners that is not visible in full-match averages.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's corner kicks AGAINST are split asymmetrically across halves (1H ~2.27, 2H ~2.87), while Team B's corner kicks FOR are more evenly split (1H ~2.35, 2H ~2.42). The joint half-level profile of Team B's corners FOR and AGAINST reveals that Team B concedes significantly more corners in the second half than the first, while generating corners more evenly. This half-level asymmetry in the FOR vs. AGAINST corner differential for Team B is a within-match structural pattern.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a within-match half-level split combined with a joint FOR vs. AGAINST differential within each half for Team B — two dimensions simultaneously. Not reducible to a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team B's fouls FOR (away venue, all-prior) as the foul-generation input, and Team A's cards_2h FOR and AGAINST (second-half, all-prior) as the disciplinary output. Also incorporate Team B's yellow_cards FOR (away vs. home split) to assess whether elevated away fouls translate into elevated second-half card accumulation when Team B plays away. Test the joint relationship across both observables simultaneously.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team B's away foul rate is elevated above its home rate, second-half cards (cards_2h) in matches involving Team B away rise above the competition context baseline, and this relationship is stronger than what either foul rate or cards_2h alone predicts.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's foul rate FOR is substantially higher away than at home (away ~12.19 vs. home ~10.11), while Team A's foul rate FOR shows minimal venue variation (home ~10.49, away ~10.88). The joint relationship between Team B's elevated away foul rate and Team A's cards_2h (second-half cards) — both teams' foul-generating tendencies combined with the second-half card accumulation pattern — creates a cross-observable, cross-team signal for second-half disciplinary activity that is not captured by either observable alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a genuine joint relationship between two distinct observables (fouls and cards_2h/yellow_cards) across two different teams, conditioned on venue, and evaluated within a specific match period (second half). It combines an asymmetric cross-team observable pairing with a within-match period split — not reducible to any single-observable mirror or single-band split.
